issues.problem: rohiṇī left as 'uncertain'. In the parallel Suśruta vessel passage the blood-carrying vessels are, to my recollection, called rohiṇī in the sense 'red', and the colours given there for the Vāta, Pitta and Kapha vessels (aruṇa; nīla/pīta; gaura) match 44-46 here. 'Red' is therefore a probable sense; wording left to the owner (the draft's hedge is safe).
issues.fix: Optionally: rohiṇī 'red (probable; literally rising, growing)' with the Hindi hedged सम्भवतः लाल.

issues.problem: Printed 'aṃgavayavā' (Deva. ंगवयवा) has no long ā; aṅga + avayava must contract to aṅgāvayava. The split aṅga-avayavāḥ silently restores it (a missing mātra), so it needs a flag.

value.why: possible: aṅga + avayava should contract to aṅgāvayava; the long ā-mātra is missing in the print (words keep the two members aṅga-avayavāḥ)

issues.problem: 'their' is not in the Sanskrit (aṅgāvayavāḥ, 'limbs and parts'; the dvandva/tat-puruṣa choice is already in the note).

A second, smaller correction exists: vahataḥ (3 du. 'carry'), one printed anusvāra away, matching the finite dual verbs of 59 and 62 ('dve ... vahataḥ'); 'dve dve' would then be 'two and two carry'. The draft's vahantyaḥ is also construable; the choice is the owner's. Translation 'carrying' reads equally for both.

patch.text: Alternative conjecture: vahataḥ (3 du., 'two and two carry'), one anusvāra off the print and parallel to the finite verbs of 59 and 62; vahantyaḥ remains possible.

issues.problem: The adopted vahantyaḥ is a correction but neither translation carries 'on a conjectural reading' (glossary: a correction adopted in a translation needs the mark in both languages). Here only the gender of a participle changes, the sense is identical, so this is left to the owner; the same applies to 65 (bhavanti).
aṣṭābhiḥ is gender-neutral by form and stands for an unstated noun: no gender in gram (glossary).
dvābhyām is gender-neutral by form and stands for an unstated noun: no gender in gram.

abhitarpayanti is rendered 'nourish' in English but literally 'satiate' in Hindi (तृप्त करती हैं); the glossary fixes tarpaṇa = satiation, and the translation should be the literal rendering with the interpretation only in notes.
Adopted bhavanti (printed bhavati) is not marked 'on a conjectural reading' in either translation; number-only change, owner decision (see 56).
The dvandva is labelled 'n.'; its last member mala is masculine (neuter only by agreement with āyatanāni), and the gender of a genitive plural dvandva should not be asserted.
Policy wants candidate identifications beside disputed terms (as done for kloma in 72); the draft gives none for mahāsrotas.

patch.text: mahāsrotas (disputed): in Caraka-type usage the great channel is the alimentary tract (koṣṭha); some commentators take the large vessels at the heart; unresolved here, so the term is kept untranslated beyond 'great channel'.

issues.problem: Glossary (p02 ch05 k5): Hindi āmāśaya = जठर, not bare पेट (पेट = udara).
English hedges jaghana ('hips or loins region, probable') but the Hindi states 'कूल्हा' unhedged and narrower; Hindi must carry the same hedge.

issues.problem: Glossary line 'majjā = kernel in all units' comes from drug chapters; here the dhātu sense 'marrow' is right. Owner should scope the glossary entry (anatomy = marrow).

summary: 41 units checked word by word against the printed lines. Draft is sound: no invented content, counts as printed (24; 10+10+4; 13; 30 = 10+8+8+4; 9 + 3), all eight text_flags plausible and marked conjectural, low-confidence units (51, 52, 61) correctly unenriched, glossary mostly followed. 2 errors fixed by patch (u64 satiate, u75 जठर) plus 11 minor items: missing flag for the silent aṅgāvayava restoration (u54), gender labels on numerals, dvandva gender (u67), unhedged Hindi jaghana (u81). Observations without patch: alternative vahataḥ for u56 (patched as note), conjectural marks for number-only corrections (u56, u65), rohiṇī possibly 'red' (u48), majjā glossary scope. Identifications all acceptably hedged; none judged wrong. The u50 'की तरह', u69 vyāyā|mavega, u72 kloma, u76 Mātrāśitīya and verb-carry choices are acceptable as drafted.
glossary_suggestions: majjā = 'kernel' in drug/plant units but 'marrow' in anatomical (dhātu) units such as p02 ch06 u82.
abhitarpayanti = 'satiate' (literal); tarpaṇa = satiation in both languages, 'nourish' only in notes.
Numerals (aṣṭābhiḥ, dvābhyām) standing for an unstated noun: case and number only in gram, no gender.
Hindi āmāśaya = जठर (p02 ch06 u75 followed).
mahāsrotas: candidates alimentary tract / large vessels, disputed; keep 'great channel'.
